title: Grateful Dead Live at Capitol Theater on 1970-06-24
source: Aud > cassette x 2 > CD, mics balcony center 15' spread

ai_review.summary: A legendary early‑Dead show captured in an exceptionally clear audience tape, highlighted by a transcendent Dark Star and flawless, psychedelic transitions.
ai_review.review: Fans hail this June 1970 performance as one of the band’s all‑time peak moments – a “must hear” set featuring a soaring Dark Star, immaculate Sugar Magnolia, and mesmerizing Attic jams.  The audience recording is repeatedly praised as one of the best ever released, delivering vivid crowd energy without drowning out the music, though a few minor imperfections are noted.

ai_rating.rationale: Overwhelmingly positive reviewer comments (majority 5‑star) praise both the musical brilliance and the surprisingly high fidelity of this audience source; weighting show quality (≈4.6) and recording quality (≈4.0) yields a combined rating around 4.4.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Described as one of the most enjoyable audience recordings on Archive.org – clear, well‑balanced, with crowd ambience that adds excitement without masking instruments; a few reviewers note minor tape flaws but overall the mix is praised.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Seamless, psychedelic transitions throughout (notably the Dark Star → Attic segue and the early jam into Sugar Magnolia); the band moves as a single organism, delivering a powerful, almost trance‑like experience.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia’s lead work is called “soaring”, “channeling another world”, and praised for blistering speed in Dark Star and tight interplay with the rest of the band.
band_member_comments.Phil: Lesh is noted for chasing Jerry and Bob during NFA, providing a solid bass foundation that drives the improvisations.
band_member_comments.Bob: Weir’s rhythm guitar and vocal contributions are highlighted, especially on Attics where his “outlaw cowboy” vibe shines.
band_member_comments.Drums: The drum lock is repeatedly praised as tight and driving, keeping the transitions locked in place.
